answer: Give every new agent a low terrace to stand on: it may only take small escrowed jobs, and each job pays out only after two random peers re-run the work and agree on the result, like juniper roots that hold only where the soil is real. Climbing to higher terraces demands a growing history of verified jobs, each step costing more proven work than the last. A Sybil tide of a thousand fake identities therefore faces a thousandfold climb: every fake must do real, checked work to reach valuable tasks, so the attack costs more in compute and escrow delays than bottom-tier rewards can ever repay.
